messages:
maria_cs: Hey team, onboarding update for AcmePayments — their integration is getting a ton of 429s at SDK init. Root cause looks like a preflight stampede from their frontend workers. Sample log: 
```
2026-03-22T14:12:03Z INFO sdk-init request_id=abc123 status=429 body=\"rate limit exceeded\" retry_after=30
2026-03-22T14:12:04Z INFO sdk-init request_id=abc124 status=429 body=\"rate limit exceeded\" retry_after=30
```

maria_cs: They spawn ~120 parallel preflight calls on cold start. Can we share quick mitigation steps we should ask them to apply?

stella_support: Oof. First quick wins: reduce parallel preflight/splay the init steps and add client-side jitter. Also confirm they're using ephemeral token TTL correctly — short TTLs cause refresh storms.

kai_integration: They are getting ephemeral tokens from our /token endpoint every time each worker spins up. TTL is 15s by default in their setup.

jon_devex: Two-pronged approach: (1) client-side: cap concurrent preflight (6-10), add backoff+jitter; (2) infra-side: temporary quota bump or a canary route to absorb initial ramp. Also enable HTTP/2 connection reuse if they aren't.

stella_support: Example client tweak to stagger and jitter initial requests: 
```
// pseudocode
const concurrencyCap = 8;
function splayedInit(workers) {
  workers.forEach((w, i) => {
    const delay = Math.min(5000, Math.floor(Math.random()*3000) + (i % concurrencyCap) * 200);
    setTimeout(() => w.preflight(), delay);
  });
}
```

maria_cs: Can we give them a short config snippet for decreasing ephemeral refresh frequency? They use the browser SDK.

jon_devex: Sure — suggest client-side token cache + refresh leeway: 
```
{ "ephemeral_token_ttl_secs": 60, "refresh_before_sec": 10, "max_parallel_refreshes": 3 }
```
Note: increasing TTL to 60s is safe for onboarding test keys; for production guide them narrower with server-side caching.

kai_integration: Are we comfortable recommending TTL 60s? Their security team might push back.

stella_support: For onboarding we can advise a temporary TTL increase for initial warmup, or they can put a tiny proxy that caches tokens for N seconds. That proxy reduces fanout without changing client security posture.

maria_cs: I'm going to ask Acme to try: 1) splay init, 2) cap parallel preflights to 8, 3) set ephemeral_token_ttl to 60 for the first 10 minutes while they warm up. Also asking for a quick runbook snippet to share with eng.

deploy-bot: Quota change applied for account_acmepayments: +50% burst quota for 1 hour (change_id=cb-20260322-01) :white_check_mark:

kai_integration: Nice — starting changes now. I'll patch their frontend to add splay and set maxParallel=8. Will report back in ~5 mins.

(30s later)

kai_integration: Patch deployed. Preflight spike now shows far fewer concurrent hits. Logs: 
```
2026-03-22T14:12:45Z INFO sdk-init request_id=abc200 status=200 body=\"ok\" latency_ms=120
2026-03-22T14:12:46Z INFO sdk-init request_id=abc201 status=200 body=\"ok\" latency_ms=110
```

maria_cs: Great — any lingering errors?

kai_integration: A couple of intermittent 429s during the first 30s but overall error rate dropped from ~18% to <1%. :thumbsup:

stella_support: OK to close this thread once they confirm stability for 1 hour. Recommend follow-up enablement: quick doc on preflight splay + token caching + a small troubleshooting checklist. I can draft.

jon_devex: I'll add a one-line snippet to the browser SDK docs about keeping persistent connections and limiting parallel preflight. Also add sample Node fetch config for keepalive: 
```
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 6 });
fetch(url, { agent });
```

maria_cs: Thanks all. I'll schedule a 15-min enablement call with Acme for tomorrow to walk through this and capture feedback for the docs.

kai_integration: Confirmed stable for 20m now. Closing on our side. Thanks! :pray:
